body:
## Goal

Make Foundryline's **Maintain** recipe as easy to adopt as its manual Discover recipe. A maintainer should be able to check a small GitHub repository's everyday engineering hygiene using RepoTend, understand which findings matter, and prepare a **reviewable, unpublished** maintenance issue when something merits attention.

**Keep Foundryline a blueprint, not a new platform.** Use RepoTend's existing read-only deterministic auditor as the check engine; do not build another rule registry, scheduler, database, general-purpose agent controller, or hosted service.

This implements [Foundryline's Milestone C](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md#3-milestone-c--maintain-reference-using-repotend), building on the [Discover runbook](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/patterns/discover.md) and [RepoTend](https://github.com/grove/repotend).

## Proposed implementation

- `patterns/maintain.md`: copyable manual procedure explaining prerequisites, the chosen pinned repository revision, trusted RepoTend installation, read-only audit invocation, findings/uncertainty, source-grounded triage, duplicate checks, and issue drafting (without remote publication).
- `examples/repo-maintenance/`: one **actually executed** RepoTend read-only audit against a documented, pinned public checkout (Foundryline itself is a useful first target), retaining commands, version/revision, JSON/Markdown outputs, limits, and any warnings/errors. Label authored fixture outputs distinctly from real receipts.
- A worked example that shows at least one useful triage outcome—or an honest no-action outcome—and a **NOT PUBLISHED** maintenance issue proposal where justified.
- Extend the existing `checks/` tests to verify links, example structure, genuine retained report identities, and that missing/failed executions are not represented as a completed audit.
- Update the welcoming README to link to Maintain once the runnable example is verified. Keep other future patterns clearly marked as planned.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] **R1 — Copyable and optional.** Another maintainer can follow `patterns/maintain.md` in a separate small GitHub repository without installing or operating Foundryline as a service. The procedure identifies actual RepoTend prerequisites (including the required Node runtime and pinned dependencies) and read-only command(s). No AI model is required for the deterministic audit.
- [ ] **R2 — Real, pinned results.** Run the actual RepoTend validator against a chosen commit and save its genuinely produced JSON/Markdown report, exact command, tool/source revision, environment and scope. No synthetic reports presented as executed outcomes; an advisory warning or no-action result is acceptable.
- [ ] **R3 — Faithful interpretation.** Preserve the actual RepoTend `PASS`, `WARN`, `FAIL`, `UNKNOWN` and `NOT_APPLICABLE` meanings, confidence (`verified` vs `heuristic`), rule IDs, applicability, and caveats. Do not call narrow static PASSes a comprehensive security verdict.
- [ ] **R4 — Read-only by default.** The Maintain audit does not execute target repository code, modify target files, call RepoTend's remediation apply path, or make GitHub issue/settings writes. Installation/setup effects occur separately and are disclosed. A report, schedule, or issue draft never grants permission to apply a fix.
- [ ] **R5 — Useful maintenance proposal.** For a finding worth acting on, consult actual relevant source/policy and any exceptions, search open and closed existing issues when permitted, and prepare an **unpublished** issue proposal with clear acceptance criteria, priority rationale, and checks labeled **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**. Otherwise report why no new issue is warranted.
- [ ] **R6 — Robust failure handling.** Exercise at least one controlled case involving missing dependencies, unavailable target source, unknown applicability, or an audit/configuration error. Report it as unavailable/unknown, not as a clean PASS. No fabricated issue URL, approval or runtime receipt.
- [ ] **R7 — Independent usability check.** Another agent/maintainer can follow the documented manual procedure, including its safety limits, using a fresh checkout or separately configured environment. Capture observed time/effort and remaining unknowns.
- [ ] **R8 — Reference checks and scope.** Existing Foundryline Python structural/reference tests pass with the new example and recipe. Documentation remains accurate about what is qualified and what is not; automatic issue creation and schedules stay future, separately tested options.

## Verification — PROPOSED — NOT RUN

1. Check out RepoTend at a recorded commit and install pinned dependencies in a trusted tool environment, separate from the target repository. Confirm the actual node/runtime versions.
2. Audit a pinned public repository read-only with RepoTend using supported commands. Retain unedited JSON/Markdown outputs and exit status; interpret warnings and unknowns without inventing repairs.
3. Review the evidence against the target repository's source/policies and relevant existing issues. Produce one actionable **NOT PUBLISHED** draft if appropriate, or an honest no-action explanation.
4. Exercise one missing-input/unknown/error case. Verify that it does not appear as a successful clean audit.
5. Ask a separately configured maintainer/agent to repeat the recipe. Retain real observations, then run `python3 -m unittest discover -s checks -v` in Foundryline and report the outcome.
6. Open an ordinary PR for review; leave issue publication, repository mutations and release decisions to authorized maintainers.

## Non-goals

No centralized Foundryline controller, scheduled automation, automatic issue creation, automatic RepoTend apply/remediation, GitHub settings mutation, universal CI/security certification, or new static-analysis engine.

**Definition of done:** A reproducible manual Maintain recipe, an actual pinned RepoTend audit with correctly reported findings/limitations, a source-grounded issue/no-action handoff, one negative control, and an independent adoption attempt, all with reviewable records.
title: feat(maintain): create a copyable manual RepoTend maintenance recipe

body:
## Goal

Foundryline's manual Discover blueprint has a real pinned-repository pilot, a fresh-agent reproduction, and an observed unavailable-source refusal. The reference tests passed, but the project still says **qualification pending maintainer review**.

Independently review the retained evidence and prepare a **reviewable PR** documenting exactly what Foundryline v0.1 can and cannot claim. The maintainer—not the coding agent—makes the final acceptance/release decision.

This is a review and release-readiness task, **not** a request to invent more pilot evidence, run RepoTend repairs, or automatically declare v0.1 qualified.

## Sources to inspect

- [Foundryline PR #5](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/pull/5) and its merged commit `36b891c29da615adf846a5d7172758ca75325f07`.
- [Live pilot record](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/examples/repotend-pilot/README.md) and the primary, reproduction, negative, and failed-launch receipts under `examples/repotend-pilot/receipts/`.
- [Pilot run-record template](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/examples/manual-discover/run-record-template.md), [manual Discover runbook](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/patterns/discover.md), [design](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/DESIGN.md), [implementation plan](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md) and existing release-status text.
- [Closed issue #4](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/issues/4) (R1–R8), [closed issue #2](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/issues/2), and [merged PR #3](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/pull/3). Closed issues are not, on their own, evidence that all checked outcomes happened.
- RepoTend source at the actual pinned commit `bfe410e4d61ddb472e335ce35877997a2f32d91f` **only insofar as needed to validate citations**; distinguish historical results from current main. Do not reproduce/write to target as a side effect of reviewing Foundryline's records.

## Review questions

1. Do the retained events, commands, reports, source manifest and code support the stated `gapline-audit` activation, bounded read-only source access, tool calls and non-execution claims? Distinguish observed effects from configured controls, agent self-reports and untested host capabilities.
2. Is the one `SUPPORTED` RepoTend finding (Markdown apply command omits the target root) adequately grounded and honestly limited to source evidence? Were applicable policies, exceptions and counterevidence preserved? No wrong-target write was reproduced.
3. Was open/closed issue deduplication actually attempted, and does the unpublished proposal correctly distinguish suspected behavior from confirmed runtime failure?
4. What does the fresh-process reproduction establish—and **not** establish—given the shared operator, runtime, provider and setup procedure? Does v0.1 need a second human or independently administered environment before qualification?
5. Was the withheld-source negative case genuinely observed, and did the agent fail closed without invented evidence or unauthorized fallback?
6. Does the missing `workflows.ts` transitive context, exposure of additional host interfaces, incomplete wrapper/provider visibility, or unknown model identity/billing require a limitation, additional check, or block?
7. Are the current README and IMPLEMENTATION release-status claims properly calibrated to the reviewed evidence?

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] **R1 — Evidence-by-criterion review.** Produce `docs/discover-v0.1-qualification-review.md` with a concise table for the original issue #4 R1–R8, each marked **SUPPORTED / PARTIAL / NOT DEMONSTRATED**, exact receipt/source pointers, counterevidence and relevant limits. Include independent reviewer process and what it could not establish.
- [ ] **R2 — Independent verification, not a rubber stamp.** Inspect and challenge original source citations, event/receipt consistency and important negative claims. Do not treat repeated model agreement, hashes, source test assertions, or green structural CI as semantic correctness or universal sandbox proof.
- [ ] **R3 — Reproduction and controls assessed accurately.** Explicitly decide whether fresh-agent reproduction with a shared operator/provider is sufficient for a **bounded host-specific** v0.1 claim, and whether further review/host tests are needed. Record refusal and capability-visibility limits without upgrading uncertain outcomes.
- [ ] **R4 — Clear release recommendation.** Recommend **QUALIFY WITH STATED SCOPE**, **REMAIN PENDING**, or **BLOCKED**, with rationale and the smallest specific additional evidence or decision required. This is advisory; it does **not** self-approve release or authenticate human acceptance.
- [ ] **R5 — Truthful documentation.** Make only warranted README, IMPLEMENTATION, and pilot-record clarification changes. Keep the project **pending maintainer acceptance** until explicitly reviewed; never silently claim all hosts or workflow automation are qualified.
- [ ] **R6 — Checks and reviewable handoff.** Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s checks -v` in Foundryline and record the real outcome. Open a PR referencing this issue, summarize observed evidence and remaining uncertainty, and leave it **unmerged** for the maintainer.

## Verification — PROPOSED — NOT RUN

- Reconcile the report against the actual PR #5 files and retained machine-readable receipts; note any record mismatch precisely.
- Cross-check the report's original requirement, selected code excerpts, exemptions and test claims against the pinned RepoTend source without executing RepoTend.
- Compare the actual independent-run/negative-run events and host restrictions with the criteria above.
- Run Foundryline's **own** structural/receipt tests if the coding-agent host permits and report the exact command/result, not an inferred pass.
- Independently review the proposed PR diff for overclaims and unintended changes.

## Non-goals and authority

Do **not** publish the provisional RepoTend issue, fix RepoTend, create more model-run receipts and call them independent, invoke an unqualified execution sandbox, create a schedule, merge a PR, or deploy. Do not alter issue #2/#4 history to suggest checks were satisfied retroactively. A coding agent may prepare evidence and a PR, but **the maintainer owns the final release/qualification decision**.

**Definition of done:** One specific, inspectable release-readiness recommendation and proposed documentation PR with honest evidence/unknowns, not an automatically certified v0.1 release.
title: Review Discover pilot evidence and prepare Foundryline v0.1 qualification decision

body:
Foundryline's manual Discover reference pattern is now documented and its structural CI checks pass, but that establishes only documentation/fixture integrity. We still need evidence that another project can use the pattern in a real coding-agent host while respecting read-only and source-authority boundaries.

This issue tracks **live qualification** of the blueprint. It follows [the merged Discover reference PR #3](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/pull/3) and [the closed blueprint issue #2](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/issues/2), whose real-host acceptance checks were not demonstrated by the structural CI run.

## Pilot target

- **Repository:** [grove/repotend](https://github.com/grove/repotend)
- **Pinned revision:** `bfe410e4d61ddb472e335ce35877997a2f32d91f` (do not silently substitute a moving `main`)
- **Investigation question:** Does RepoTend's remediation implementation preserve the documented preview/read-only behavior, explicit approval requirement, stale-plan handling, and protection against overwriting existing files?
- **Initial inspection scope:** `docs/REMEDIATION.md`, `skills/repotend/scripts/remediation.ts`, `test/remediation.test.mjs`, plus only necessary permitted callers/configuration to assess counterevidence.
- **Procedure:** [Foundryline patterns/discover.md](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/patterns/discover.md); record actual observations using [run-record-template.md](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/examples/manual-discover/run-record-template.md).

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] **R1 — Qualified setup and actual invocation.** Record the agent host and version, installed skill/revision, verified *actual* `gapline-audit` activation, source revision, selected paths, access controls and inspection budget. Skill installation or reading skill text alone is not sufficient evidence.
- [ ] **R2 — Bounded, read-only pilot.** Perform a real Gapline investigation against the fixed RepoTend revision with host-enforced read-only scope. Retain available host activity/permission evidence. The Gapline stage must not execute project code, tests or builds, write repository files, create issues/PRs, or invoke unsafe shell/network operations; disclose any visibility limitations rather than claiming stronger isolation than observed.
- [ ] **R3 — Evidence-calibrated report.** Return zero to three consequential findings, with exact source paths/lines, supporting and counterevidence, appropriate evidence level, scoped impact, unassessed areas and falsifying observations marked **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**. A justified no-findings outcome is valid; source inspection does not establish a runtime failure.
- [ ] **R4 — Original-source and duplicate triage.** Trace any proposed obligations to RepoTend's applicable documented behavior and exceptions; distinguish accepted promises from suggestions/tests/current implementation. Check related existing **open and closed** issues where available and record search coverage and uncertain duplicates.
- [ ] **R5 — Provisional issue handoff.** For a sufficiently supported lead, use `intentline-issue` *drafting guidance* to return a **NOT PUBLISHED** issue proposal with plain-language context, source-grounded acceptance criteria, explicit evidence gaps, and **PROPOSED — NOT RUN** verification. An unconfirmed runtime concern starts with **Confirm before fixing**. If no finding qualifies, publish no proposal. No remote issue CREATE/UPDATE or saved `intentline-plan` record is authorized by this pilot.
- [ ] **R6 — Independent reproduction.** A second maintainer or independently configured agent follows the same pinned inputs and runbook. Record its actual skill invocation, independent observations, important differences, evidence quality, tool usage and costs where available. Identical findings are **not** required.
- [ ] **R7 — Witnessed negative/refusal case.** On a separately arranged safe control run, deliberately make a necessary source/host capability unavailable (or introduce an unresolved authority gap), and observe correct refusal/qualified provisional output. Record the **actual** response without fabricated citations, findings, approvals or executed-test claims.
- [ ] **R8 — Honest qualification and retention.** Store a reviewable pilot record, independent reproduction, negative-path result, elapsed time and model/tool cost where measurable, and explicit unknowns. Preserve private source/output as private. Do not label v0.1 live-qualified unless the relevant evidence is present and reviewed.

## Verification — PROPOSED — NOT RUN

1. Pin and document RepoTend's exact commit and applicable policy files. Verify the actual agent-host environment and read-only capabilities before starting.
2. Run the bounded `gapline-audit` pilot and review source references and counterevidence independently. Do not treat proposed probes as executed tests.
3. Use `intentline-issue` guidance to prepare an unpublished issue proposal if justified; check that expected behavior comes from applicable originals and duplicate issue checks are reported.
4. Repeat using a separately configured agent or second maintainer. Preserve actual differences, attempts, refusals and usage.
5. Exercise and inspect an explicit unavailable-capability/refusal case, with read-only boundaries enforced by the host rather than instructions alone.
6. Review retained records against R1–R8 and clearly qualify what was and was not demonstrated.

## Non-goals

No Foundryline controller, scheduled job, automatic issue creation, project repairs, tests executed under the Gapline stage, PR publication, merge, deployment, universal host isolation certification, or mandatory saved acceptance agreement. Any later implementation/proof requires separate authorization and qualified execution.

**Definition of done:** One actual, bounded pilot (including a valid no-findings outcome if appropriate), one independently reproduced procedure, and one observed negative/refusal run have been reviewed with accurate scope, provenance, uncertainty, and costs where available.
title: Qualify manual Discover with a real RepoTend pilot and independent reproduction

body:
## Problem and objective

Foundryline v0.1 needs to demonstrate that another project can adopt a **manual, read-only Discover pattern** using existing coding-agent skills—without requiring a Foundryline service, controller, database, or custom runtime.

The intended outcome is a reproducible, evidence-grounded investigation that produces a useful **NOT PUBLISHED** issue proposal (or an honest no-findings result), without silently turning audit hypotheses into confirmed defects, approved requirements, or authorized changes.

This implements the first milestone in [IMPLEMENTATION.md](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/IMPLEMENTATION.md#1-milestone-a--manual-discover-reference-first-usable-deliverable), following [DESIGN.md](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/blob/main/DESIGN.md). The checklist below is the proposed v0.1 release gate.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- [ ] **R1 — Copyable setup.** A maintainer can follow documented instructions in a fresh repository with existing coding-agent skills. No Foundryline service, controller, database, or custom runtime is required.
- [ ] **R2 — Actual Gapline invocation.** Run `gapline-audit` through a supported, real coding-agent host against a repository with an identified Git revision. Record host, tool/skill versions, inspected scope, and available budgets. Merely installing a skill does not satisfy this criterion.
- [ ] **R3 — Read-only boundary.** Check actual host permissions/activity records for the audit. No project code, tests, or builds execute; no repository files change; no issue-tracker writes occur. Do not treat agent instructions alone as an isolation guarantee.
- [ ] **R4 — Evidence-calibrated findings.** Retain a report with **zero to three** findings, each with precise source references, support, counterevidence, evidence level, limitations and next discriminating observation. State what was not inspected. **Zero supported findings is valid.**
- [ ] **R5 — Source verification and deduplication.** For consequential leads, inspect applicable original requirements/documented behavior and accepted exceptions, plus related open **and closed** issues when accessible. Do not convert an unsupported hypothesis into a confirmed bug or silently create new product obligations.
- [ ] **R6 — Actionable issue proposal.** Use `intentline-issue` guidance to prepare a **NOT PUBLISHED** issue proposal with a plain-language problem statement, source-grounded proposed acceptance criteria, and verification labeled **PROPOSED — NOT RUN**. Suspected runtime defects require **confirm before fixing**. If nothing qualifies, retain a no-findings outcome instead.
- [ ] **R7 — Optional acceptance planning.** Document when to use and skip `intentline-plan`. Saving a formal agreement requires a separately authorized operation, permitted original source bytes, a compatible installed Intentline runtime, and safe private storage. A saved DRAFT is not external approval or proof. Issue drafting/creation alone does not imply a saved record.
- [ ] **R8 — Failure/refusal behavior.** Exercise at least one negative case (for example missing authoritative behavior, inaccessible source/issue inventory, unavailable host capability, or absent safe execution boundary). Record the limitation instead of inventing findings, receipts, identities or permissions.
- [ ] **R9 — Independent reproduction.** A second maintainer or independently configured agent can follow the instructions and reproduce the **procedure**, recording observations, deviations, elapsed time, and available model/tool usage. Identical findings are not required; consistent evidence and safety standards are.

## Deliverables

- `patterns/discover.md`: complete manual runbook, input/scope contract, invocation, triage, deduplication, output states, and explicit authorization boundaries.
- `examples/manual-discover/`: clearly identified authored examples for a finding and for no findings/refusal. Keep fixtures separate from observed real-host evidence.
- At least one **actual** read-only pilot on a pinned public repository revision, with host/skill activation evidence and honest report.
- An independent reproduction and a documented negative-path check, with actual outcome, time/cost where available and any unresolved limits.

## Verification — PROPOSED — NOT RUN

1. Independently follow the setup and manual Discover recipe on a known, pinned repository snapshot. Verify actual tool/skill activation and what was inspected.
2. Examine source citations, counterevidence and applicable original requirements/exceptions; review both open and closed potential duplicate issues.
3. Examine the proposed issue body (or honest no-findings result), confirm `NOT PUBLISHED` and `PROPOSED — NOT RUN` markings, and verify no unsupported runtime claims.
4. Review actual host activity against the read-only boundary; exercise a missing-prerequisite/authority case and confirm a refusal or appropriately provisional result.
5. Record the independent replication attempt, failures, limitations and usage/cost information when available.

Passing Markdown/link validation alone is **not** sufficient evidence of a real agent run, isolation or usefulness.

## Definition of done

**v0.1 can be called a usable manual Discover blueprint only when one genuine pilot, one independent reproduction and one negative-path exercise satisfy the applicable criteria with observed evidence.** A correct no-findings result does not block release.

## Out of scope

Scheduled execution, automatic issue publication, autonomous implementation, PR creation, mutation testing, central orchestration, end-to-end proof, and deployment. Those are later, separately qualified and authorized patterns.
title: Qualify Foundryline v0.1 manual Discover blueprint
